messages:
alex: quick heads-up, PR #8572 seems to have introduced a small-batch throughput regression on the 1k-seq workloads. see attached bench run: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/bench/4073/8572-small-batch
mira: :eyes: can you paste the bench numbers here? CI link is flaky for me from home
alex: sure. from the CI artifact (avg of 5 runs):
- master: throughput=380 tok/s, p95=48ms, p50=20ms
- pr-8572: throughput=300 tok/s, p95=82ms, p50=22ms
so overall throughput down ~21% and tail doubled on this config
jon: that's pretty visible. did you re-run with caching disabled? could be a KV-cache interaction
alex: ran with cache enabled (same as prod). re-ran with --no-kv-cache and numbers are closer: throughput=365 tok/s, p95=50ms. looks like the change affects cache behavior under small batches
sam: can you share the exact command you ran? i'll reproduce locally
alex: command i used:
```bash
./bench/run_small_batch.sh --model redwood/vicuna-13b-q4 --seq 1024 --batch 4 --runs 5
```

also artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/bench/4073/8572-small-batch/logs.tar.gz
pat: quick skim of the diff — PR touches scheduler heuristics + kv-sharding. i'm worried the new shard rebalancer is adding latency when cache miss patterns are bursty
mira: pinging @jon and @sam for a second perf pass. can someone try toggling shard_rebalance=false and see impact?
jon: running now on my workstation, will post numbers in ~10m
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: pr-8572 -> canary cluster (3 nodes) at 2026-03-17T03:08:40Z
sre-oncall: FYI if canary is noisy let me know; i'll pause ramp
sam: repro'd locally:
- with shard_rebalance=true (PR): throughput=305 tok/s, p95=80ms
- with shard_rebalance=false: throughput=378 tok/s, p95=46ms
so disabling rebalance restores perf almost to master
alex: thanks sam — that matches my suspicion. looks like rebalance is misrouting requests for small batches
pat: i can take a quick follow-up: limit rebalance to >batch_size 8 or add cooldown. simpler guard might avoid the regression
mira: do we want a hotfix on top of this PR or revert and rework? what's the risk surface
jon: if we revert it's low-risk and buys time. if we hotfix, i can add the guard in a small patch and run canary again
alex: prefer hotfix guard + canary if we can get a quick patch. can someone open a follow-up branch and assign reviewers?
sam: i'll open pr-8572.1 with the guard; benching now then will push
alex: cheers. assign to @mira + @jon for perf + correctness review. leave deploy-bot on canary hold until we see bench confirms
mira: :thumbsup: once sam posts bench from the patched run i'll give the quick perf ok
sam: patched and pushed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8572.1
bench (5 runs): throughput=374 tok/s, p95=49ms, p50=21ms
alex: looks good to me. canary resume?
sre-oncall: resume canary, watching. will alert if tail jumps >2x baseline
deploy-bot: canary resumed for pr-8572 at 2026-03-17T03:22:30Z
jon: approved the follow-up (quick perf pass). leaving final lgtm to @mira for correctness
mira: left comments on one edge-case; otherwise lgtm for the guard. suggest follow-up issue to audit rebalance heuristics across batch sizes
alex: thanks all. documenting next steps in PR and adding a perf regression alert test for small-batch cases. will close thread after merge
pat: nice catch, alex. saved a lot of noisy canary alerts :rocket:
